requirements_xml:
<requirements_list>
  <requirement id="R1">
    <category>Existence</category>
    <description>The background-blend-mode CSS property must exist and be supported.</description>
    <spec_quote>| Name: | background-blend-mode |</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R2">
    <category>Existence</category>
    <description>The background-blend-mode CSS property must accept a comma-separated list of one or more <'mix-blend-mode'> values.</description>
    <spec_quote>| Value: | [<'mix-blend-mode'>](#propdef-mix-blend-mode)# |</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R3">
    <category>Existence</category>
    <description>The <'mix-blend-mode'> value accepted by background-blend-mode must support <blend-mode> values and the plus-lighter keyword.</description>
    <spec_quote>| Value: | [<blend-mode>](#ltblendmodegt) | [plus-lighter](#plus-lighter) |</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R4">
    <category>Existence</category>
    <description>The <blend-mode> value type accepted by background-blend-mode must support the keywords normal, darken, multiply, color-burn, lighten, screen, color-dodge, overlay, soft-light, hard-light, difference, exclusion, hue, saturation, color, and luminosity.</description>
    <spec_quote><blend-mode> =
  normal |
  darken | multiply | color-burn |
  lighten | screen | color-dodge |
  overlay | soft-light | hard-light |
  difference | exclusion |
  hue | saturation | color | luminosity</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R5">
    <category>Existence</category>
    <description>The background-blend-mode CSS property must accept the inherit keyword as its property value.</description>
    <spec_quote>In addition to the property-specific values listed in their definitions,
all properties defined in this specification also accept the inherit
keyword as their property value.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R6">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Each background layer of an element with `background-blend-mode` applied must blend with the background layer below it and with the element's `background-color`.</description>
    <spec_quote>Each background layer must blend with the element’s background layer that is below it and the element’s background color.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R7">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>An element's background layers must act as if rendered into an isolated group and must not blend with content rendered behind the element.</description>
    <spec_quote>Background layers must not blend with the content that is behind the element, instead they must act as if they are rendered into an isolated group.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R8">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Because background layers act as an isolated group, the initial backdrop used for compositing the bottommost background layer must be black and fully transparent.</description>
    <spec_quote>In an isolated group, the initial backdrop shall be black and fully transparent.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R9">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Each CSS background image must itself be rendered into an isolated group so its internal artwork does not blend directly with underlying background layers or the element's background color.</description>
    <spec_quote>In CSS, a background image or the content of an img must always be rendered into an isolated group.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R10">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>The comma-separated list of blend modes in `background-blend-mode` must be applied to background layers in the same order as `background-image`, with the first value applying to the topmost background layer.</description>
    <spec_quote>The [background-blend-mode](#propdef-background-blend-mode) list must be applied in the same order as background-image [[CSS3BG]](#biblio-css3bg "CSS Backgrounds and Borders Module Level 3"). This means that the first element in the list will apply to the layer that is on top.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R11">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When `background-blend-mode` specifies fewer comma-separated values than the number of background layers, the user agent must determine the used value by repeating the list of values until every background layer has a blend mode.</description>
    <spec_quote>If a property doesn’t have enough comma-separated values to match the number of layers, the UA must calculate its used value by repeating the list of values until there are enough.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R12">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When the `background` shorthand property is declared on an element, the element's `background-blend-mode` property must be reset to its initial value (`normal`).</description>
    <spec_quote>If the background [[CSS3BG]](#biblio-css3bg "CSS Backgrounds and Borders Module Level 3") shorthand is used, the [background-blend-mode](#propdef-background-blend-mode)
property for that element must be reset to its initial value.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R13">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>The `background-blend-mode` property must accept a comma-separated list of one or more `<'mix-blend-mode'>` values (`<blend-mode>` keywords or `plus-lighter`).</description>
    <spec_quote>| Name: | background-blend-mode |
| Value: | [<'mix-blend-mode'>](#propdef-mix-blend-mode)# |</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R14">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When `background-blend-mode` is not specified on an element, its initial value must be `normal`.</description>
    <spec_quote>| Value: | [<'mix-blend-mode'>](#propdef-mix-blend-mode)# |
| Initial: | normal |</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R15">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>The `background-blend-mode` property must apply to all HTML elements.</description>
    <spec_quote>| Applies to: | All HTML elements |</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R16">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>The `background-blend-mode` property must not be inherited by descendant elements by default.</description>
    <spec_quote>| Applies to: | All HTML elements |
| Inherited: | no |</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R17">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>The `background-blend-mode` property must accept the `inherit` keyword as a valid property value.</description>
    <spec_quote>all properties defined in this specification also accept the inherit
keyword as their property value.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R18">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>The computed value of `background-blend-mode` must be the value as specified.</description>
    <spec_quote>| Computed value: | as specified |</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R19">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Animating the `background-blend-mode` property must use discrete animation.</description>
    <spec_quote>| Animation type: | discrete |</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R20">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Blending calculations for background layers must operate on non-premultiplied color values rather than pre-multiplied color values.</description>
    <spec_quote>The blending calculations must not use pre-multiplied color values.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R21">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When blending a background layer onto a backdrop with alpha `αb`, the blended color must be modulated by the backdrop alpha according to `Cr = (1 - αb) x Cs + αb x B(Cb, Cs)`.</description>
    <spec_quote>The value of the new color becomes:

```
Cr = (1 - αb) x Cs + αb x B(Cb, Cs)
```</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R22">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When `background-blend-mode` is set to `normal`, the blending function must select the source color directly (`B(Cb, Cs) = Cs`) with no blending.</description>
    <spec_quote>#### 10.1.1. normal blend mode

This is the default attribute which specifies no blending. The blending formula simply selects the source color.

```
B(Cb, Cs) = Cs
```</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R23">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When `background-blend-mode` is set to `multiply`, the blending function must multiply each source color component by the corresponding backdrop color component (`B(Cb, Cs) = Cb x Cs`).</description>
    <spec_quote>#### 10.1.2. multiply blend mode

The source color is multiplied by the destination color and replaces the destination.

The resultant color is always at least as dark as either the source or destination color. Multiplying any color with black results in black. Multiplying any color with white preserves the original color.

```
B(Cb, Cs) = Cb x Cs
```</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R24">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When `background-blend-mode` is set to `screen`, the blending function must multiply the complements of each backdrop and source color component and complement the result (`B(Cb, Cs) = 1 - [(1 - Cb) x (1 - Cs)]`).</description>
    <spec_quote>#### 10.1.3. screen blend mode

Multiplies the complements of the [backdrop](#backdrop) and source color values, then complements the result.

The result color is always at least as light as either of the two constituent colors. Screening any color with white produces white; screening with black leaves the original color unchanged. The effect is similar to projecting multiple photographic slides simultaneously onto a single screen.

```
B(Cb, Cs) = 1 - [(1 - Cb) x (1 - Cs)]
          = Cb + Cs -(Cb x Cs)
```</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R25">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When `background-blend-mode` is set to `overlay`, the blending function must apply `HardLight(Cs, Cb)` per color component, multiplying or screening depending on the backdrop color component value.</description>
    <spec_quote>#### 10.1.4. overlay blend mode

Multiplies or screens the colors, depending on the [backdrop](#backdrop) color value.

Source colors overlay the [backdrop](#backdrop) while preserving its highlights and shadows. The backdrop color is not replaced but is mixed with the source color to reflect the lightness or darkness of the backdrop.

```
B(Cb, Cs) = HardLight(Cs, Cb)
```</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R26">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When `background-blend-mode` is set to `darken`, the blending function must select the minimum of the backdrop and source color values for each component (`B(Cb, Cs) = min(Cb, Cs)`).</description>
    <spec_quote>#### 10.1.5. darken blend mode

Selects the darker of the [backdrop](#backdrop) and source colors.

The [backdrop](#backdrop) is replaced with the source where the source is darker; otherwise, it is left unchanged.

```
B(Cb, Cs) = min(Cb, Cs)
```</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R27">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When `background-blend-mode` is set to `lighten`, the blending function must select the maximum of the backdrop and source color values for each component (`B(Cb, Cs) = max(Cb, Cs)`).</description>
    <spec_quote>#### 10.1.6. lighten blend mode

Selects the lighter of the [backdrop](#backdrop) and source colors.

The [backdrop](#backdrop) is replaced with the source where the source is lighter; otherwise, it is left unchanged.

```
B(Cb, Cs) = max(Cb, Cs)
```</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R28">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When `background-blend-mode` is set to `color-dodge`, the blending function must compute `0` if `Cb == 0`, `1` if `Cs == 1`, and `min(1, Cb / (1 - Cs))` otherwise for each color component.</description>
    <spec_quote>#### 10.1.7. color-dodge blend mode

Brightens the [backdrop](#backdrop) color to reflect the source color. Painting with black produces no changes.

```
if(Cb == 0)
    B(Cb, Cs) = 0
else if(Cs == 1)
    B(Cb, Cs) = 1
else
    B(Cb, Cs) = min(1, Cb / (1 - Cs))
```</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R29">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When `background-blend-mode` is set to `color-burn`, the blending function must compute `1` if `Cb == 1`, `0` if `Cs == 0`, and `1 - min(1, (1 - Cb) / Cs)` otherwise for each color component.</description>
    <spec_quote>#### 10.1.8. color-burn blend mode

Darkens the [backdrop](#backdrop) color to reflect the source color. Painting with white produces no change.

```
if(Cb == 1)
    B(Cb, Cs) = 1
else if(Cs == 0)
    B(Cb, Cs) = 0
else
    B(Cb, Cs) = 1 - min(1, (1 - Cb) / Cs)
```</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R30">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When `background-blend-mode` is set to `hard-light`, the blending function must compute `Multiply(Cb, 2 x Cs)` when `Cs <= 0.5` and `Screen(Cb, 2 x Cs - 1)` otherwise for each color component.</description>
    <spec_quote>#### 10.1.9. hard-light blend mode

Multiplies or screens the colors, depending on the source color value. The effect is similar to shining a harsh spotlight on the [backdrop](#backdrop).

```
if(Cs <= 0.5)
    B(Cb, Cs) = Multiply(Cb, 2 x Cs)
else
    B(Cb, Cs) = Screen(Cb, 2 x Cs -1)
```</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R31">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When `background-blend-mode` is set to `soft-light`, the blending function must compute `Cb - (1 - 2 x Cs) x Cb x (1 - Cb)` when `Cs <= 0.5`, and `Cb + (2 x Cs - 1) x (D(Cb) - Cb)` otherwise, where `D(Cb)` is `((16 * Cb - 12) x Cb + 4) x Cb` for `Cb <= 0.25` and `sqrt(Cb)` otherwise.</description>
    <spec_quote>#### 10.1.10. soft-light blend mode

Darkens or lightens the colors, depending on the source color value. The effect is similar to shining a diffused spotlight on the [backdrop](#backdrop).

```
    if(Cs <= 0.5)
        B(Cb, Cs) = Cb - (1 - 2 x Cs) x Cb x (1 - Cb)
    else
        B(Cb, Cs) = Cb + (2 x Cs - 1) x (D(Cb) - Cb)
with
    if(Cb <= 0.25)
        D(Cb) = ((16 * Cb - 12) x Cb + 4) x Cb
    else
        D(Cb) = sqrt(Cb)
```</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R32">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When `background-blend-mode` is set to `difference`, the blending function must compute the absolute difference between the backdrop and source color components (`B(Cb, Cs) = | Cb - Cs |`).</description>
    <spec_quote>#### 10.1.11. difference blend mode

Subtracts the darker of the two constituent colors from the lighter color.

Painting with white inverts the [backdrop](#backdrop) color; painting with black produces no change.

```
B(Cb, Cs) = | Cb - Cs |
```</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R33">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When `background-blend-mode` is set to `exclusion`, the blending function must compute `Cb + Cs - 2 x Cb x Cs` for each color component.</description>
    <spec_quote>#### 10.1.12. exclusion blend mode

Produces an effect similar to that of the Difference mode but lower in contrast. Painting with white inverts the [backdrop](#backdrop) color; painting with black produces no change

```
B(Cb, Cs) = Cb + Cs - 2 x Cb x Cs
```</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R34">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When `background-blend-mode` is set to `hue`, the non-separable blending function must produce a color with the hue of the source color and the saturation and luminosity of the backdrop color using `SetLum(SetSat(Cs, Sat(Cb)), Lum(Cb))`.</description>
    <spec_quote>#### 10.2.1. hue blend mode

Creates a color with the hue of the source color and the saturation and luminosity of the [backdrop](#backdrop) color.

```
B(Cb, Cs) = SetLum(SetSat(Cs, Sat(Cb)), Lum(Cb))
```</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R35">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When `background-blend-mode` is set to `saturation`, the non-separable blending function must produce a color with the saturation of the source color and the hue and luminosity of the backdrop color using `SetLum(SetSat(Cb, Sat(Cs)), Lum(Cb))`.</description>
    <spec_quote>#### 10.2.2. saturation blend mode

Creates a color with the saturation of the source color and the hue and luminosity of the [backdrop](#backdrop) color. Painting with this mode in an area of the backdrop that is a pure gray (no saturation) produces no change.

```
B(Cb, Cs) = SetLum(SetSat(Cb, Sat(Cs)), Lum(Cb))
```</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R36">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When `background-blend-mode` is set to `color`, the non-separable blending function must produce a color with the hue and saturation of the source color and the luminosity of the backdrop color using `SetLum(Cs, Lum(Cb))`.</description>
    <spec_quote>#### 10.2.3. color blend mode

Creates a color with the hue and saturation of the source color and the luminosity of the [backdrop](#backdrop) color. This preserves the gray levels of the backdrop and is useful for coloring monochrome images or tinting color images.

```
B(Cb, Cs) = SetLum(Cs, Lum(Cb))
```</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R37">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When `background-blend-mode` is set to `luminosity`, the non-separable blending function must produce a color with the luminosity of the source color and the hue and saturation of the backdrop color using `SetLum(Cb, Lum(Cs))`.</description>
    <spec_quote>#### 10.2.4. luminosity blend mode

Creates a color with the luminosity of the source color and the hue and saturation of the [backdrop](#backdrop) color. This produces an inverse effect to that of the Color mode.

```
B(Cb, Cs) = SetLum(Cb, Lum(Cs))
```</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R38">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When `background-blend-mode` is set to `plus-lighter`, the background layer must be composited with the backdrop using `co = min(1, αs x Cs + αb x Cb)` and `αo = min(1, αs + αb)`.</description>
    <spec_quote>#### 9.1.15. Plus-lighter

With the plus-lighter compositing operator, the following steps are performed:

```
Fa = 1; Fb = 1
co = min(1, αs x Cs + αb x Cb);
αo = min(1, αs + αb);
```</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R39">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>The comma-separated list of values specified for `background-blend-mode` must be mapped to background layers in the same order as the `background-image` property from CSS Backgrounds and Borders, such that the first blend mode applies to the topmost background layer.</description>
    <spec_quote>The [background-blend-mode](#propdef-background-blend-mode) list must be applied in the same order as background-image [[CSS3BG]](#biblio-css3bg "CSS Backgrounds and Borders Module Level 3").</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R40">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When `background-blend-mode` specifies fewer comma-separated values than the number of background layers defined by `background-image`, the used value must be computed by repeating the `background-blend-mode` list until there are enough values to match all background layers.</description>
    <spec_quote>If a property doesn’t have enough comma-separated values to match the number of layers, the UA must calculate its used value by repeating the list of values until there are enough.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R41">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When the CSS `background` shorthand property is declared on an element, the element's `background-blend-mode` property must be reset to its initial value (`normal`).</description>
    <spec_quote>If the background [[CSS3BG]](#biblio-css3bg "CSS Backgrounds and Borders Module Level 3") shorthand is used, the [background-blend-mode](#propdef-background-blend-mode)
property for that element must be reset to its initial value.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R42">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>An element's background layers blended via `background-blend-mode` must act as if rendered into an isolated compositing group and must not blend with content rendered behind the element.</description>
    <spec_quote>Background layers must not blend with the content that is behind the element, instead they must act as if they are rendered into an isolated group.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
</requirements_list>
